notes:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Northpeak AI is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for their production “support agent” workload (streaming chat + tool calls + retrieval). Primary ask: predictable throughput under peak bursts; they’ve been burned by noisy-neighbor + autoscale lag on their current self-hosted stack.
- Strongly prefers Dedicated with VPC connectivity. Hosted API is being used only for early prototyping.

CURRENT STAGE / DEAL HEALTH
- Stage: Evaluation (technical deep dive completed; procurement prep starting).
- Health: Yellow → Green pending tier launch artifacts (throughput SLO definition + contract language) and EU capacity confirmation.

KEY REQUIREMENTS (from calls + notes)
Throughput / performance
- Quote from Eng: “We need an actual number we can plan around, not ‘best effort’.”
- Target capacity (their words): ~8k–12k output tokens/sec sustained during business hours, with bursts ~1.5–2x at shift change.
- Concurrency: typical 80–120 concurrent chats; peaks 200+ for short windows.
- Workload shape: heavy streaming (token-by-token) + occasional long responses (summaries) at end of case.
- Latency guardrails (informal): p95 time-to-first-token < 1.2–1.8s for common prompts; “don’t care about absolute p99 as long as we don’t stall streaming.”
- They specifically asked how Redwood defines throughput with mixed prompt sizes + streaming (need our measurement/exclusions spelled out).

Region / residency
- Primary region: us-east.
- Secondary: EU (eu-west preferred). Requirement is “EU customers can’t leave EU” for one segment; they’re trying to avoid a separate self-hosted EU deployment.
- Will accept phased rollout if EU Dedicated capacity is committed on a timeline.

Security / compliance
- Needs: SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs for admin actions, retention controls (log retention <= 14–30 days for some tenants), and a SOC2 package.
- VPC connectivity: wants private networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink-style) + IP allowlisting.

Model / routing
- Currently testing a mix of open models (Llama-family + rerankers). They want the ability to pin versions and do canary rollouts.
- Interested in “fallback model” behavior only if it’s explicit/contracted (they don’t want silent quality changes during load).

ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2025-01-29: Inbound from Northpeak via website form (“Dedicated capacity + throughput guarantee”).
- 2025-02-03: Intro call (Jordan). Confirmed Dedicated interest, asked for token/sec commitment and regional availability.
- 2025-02-13: Technical deep dive (Fireflies: ff-2025-02-13-northpeak-technical-deep-dive). Mina + Omar joined. Main topics: tokens/sec vs req/sec, streaming impact, backlog/queue depth, and how admission control works.
- 2025-02-19: Follow-up email thread re: SLA language and whether we can offer “exception” throughput above the planned tiers (referenced in internal SLA exception request thread).

- Need to align on measurement assumptions:
  - What context length distribution will be used for the guarantee?

  - Whether guarantee is “sustained tokens/sec over N-minute window” (their preference) vs per-request.
- EU dedicated H100/A100 availability is the biggest risk. If EU is hard requirement, may need alternative shape (L4) or staged commitment.
- They asked for remedies/credits if we miss throughput guarantee (procurement will push for something explicit).
